title: Postmortem: Percentile-misaligned scaling metric caused warm-pool starvation and cascading cold-starts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a traffic spike in EU-region serving, the HPA/KEDA control loop misinterpreted a short high-percentile latency signal as sustained load. This drove an aggressive scale-down of our warm-pool and prevented warm instances from being provisioned fast enough, resulting in cascading cold-starts and elevated latency for customer-facing inference endpoints. The incident lasted ~47 minutes and impacted a subset of hosted customers in eu-west-1 with latency SLO breaches and increased token-cost per request.

impact: Duration: 47 minutes. Affected customers: ~12 hosted projects in eu-west-1 (internal tag: retail-*, analytics-*). Symptoms: p95 latency increased to 520ms (baseline ~180ms), 4x increase in cold-start error rates for batched requests, and token cost per successful request rose ~12% during the event. No data loss or security exposure.
detection_and_response: Detection relied on synthetic p95 alarms and route-level SLO monitors. Initial response focused on GPU queue analysis; the warm-pool metric anomaly was not recognized until correlating KEDA/HPA events with instance lifecycle logs. The on-call team executed a manual capacity override and reverted a recent percentile-aggregation tweak pushed earlier that morning. Post-rollback, the warm-pool recovered and latency normalized.
root_cause: A recent change to the HPA/KEDA metric aggregation switched the scaler's signal from 'observed 90th-percentile over 1m' to a blended 95th-percentile over 30s with no additional smoothing. Short-lived client-side request spikes produced transient high-percentile samples that the scaler treated as sustained load, triggering asymmetric scale decisions. Because warm-pool shrink/grow latencies are larger than the 30s sampling window, the control loop oscillated and effectively starved warm capacity before the system could replenish it. Contributing factors: (1) aggregation window too narrow for our warm-pool dynamics, (2) lack of probe gating for warm-pool eviction, (3) insufficient synthetic load tests exercising high-percentile bursts during canary, and (4) no dashboard showing percentile sample-rate anomalies to correlate with autoscaler decisions.
mitigations_executed: Rolled back the morning metric-aggregation change within 6 minutes of detection
Manually increased warm-pool target by +40% to restore capacity
Temporarily disabled aggressive scale-down policy while root-cause analysis completed
Added a short-lived rule to mute percentile-triggered scale-downs for 10 minutes following a scale-up
action_items: (A-1) Change HPA/KEDA aggregation to blended percentile with configurable smoothing: switch default to p95 over 3m with 60s EWMA; owner: Marcus Liu; due: 2026-03-15; status: in progress

follow_up_notes: We observed earlier near-miss events in January with similar sample-rate anomalies; these were not escalated because latency SLOs remained within target. We will revisit near-miss criteria.
The recent merge that changed aggregation had no canary with synthetic percentile bursts; add minimum test coverage for aggregation changes.
Consider exposing a public-facing status note for impacted customers with optional opt-in alerts when warm-pool capacity falls below threshold.
